reason: Changing a control on the Metaform web page (menu, select, dialog, setting the page reads) and its browser tests went through several failure points: a removed id still used by a test, a 400 refusal logged as a console error that the test's problems list did not expect, a shared uncommitted page tree, and a subagent handed the fix. No existing skill covers the web page, so this is the class-level home for the next UI change.
Episode fixed a figure bug in agents.js after a browser test timed out at wait_for_function; the skill covers page and browser test work but lacks the figure-state rule and the stale-page note.

The episode repeatedly lost time to stale state: a running web server kept old Python code, an open tab kept old JS, a per-project figure list was not cleared on project switch, and a 2D copy of a 3D rule was missed. The skill already covers the open-tab case; these are the missing steps.

A diagram or MCP view that grows after its thread row is placed pushes the newest line out of view when the person has the thread pinned. Re-follow the end after the growth, guarded by the pinned state.
A browser test seeded a tool-call record by hand, so it passed while the page got less than the real runner sends. Build the seeded shape from the real command's JSON output instead.
Mermaid fences in chat text had no written rule. The parse-before-render, DOMParser and source-keyed cache choices came from this session and should carry forward to any later diagram work.

Another session rewrote board.js mid-ticket and the agent's edit was silently lost; the fix had to be re-applied on the other session's version. The page tree is shared, so a post-edit check is the only way to know the edit landed.

renderBoard assigned B.tickets before the project/base freshness check, so a slow read for a previous base could overwrite the board of the base now shown. The fix moved the assignment after the guard; this is a rule for every async page handler.

Two checks the agent had to improvise this run: node --check does not catch a moved export's missing import, and isolating an unrelated browser failure needs a file-copy procedure (no stash on a shared tree). Both belong in the page-change rules.
A browser test timed out because the agent doubled the #settings prefix that row() already carries; the section heading structure is also needed to write the locator.
The agent isolated its new steps from a pre-existing failure by slicing the test and restoring from a copy. That is a reusable procedure, and the skill covers only the page-file version of it.
Absorbed into the metaform-development umbrella; full body carried verbatim into references/web-page-changes.md.
